sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Felix is an expanding water, waste-treatment and recycling platform, not yet an evidence-backed compounder. FY26 group revenue reached ₹102.21 crore and reported PAT ₹18.18 crore, but CFO was −₹36.59 crore and large advances/capital-creditor claims remain central. At ₹188, current-share TTM owner P/E is 15.87×; this does not resolve cash access or minority economics. BQS 5.18, GQS 5.00 after the cash cap, IAS NS. The funded conditional base yields 11.07% against 15%, but assumes ₹39.80 crore new debt and unresolved subsidiary attribution. Hold for funding and cash/NCI evidence, not a default finding. sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Felix Industries Limited, ISIN INE901X01013, NSE SME FELIX. Cutoff 20 October 2026; official market session 19 October. Price ₹188 and 17,206,350 actual shares imply ₹323.47938 crore market capitalization. The September 21 main-board migration filing is an application, not completion; current traded series is SM. Historical group scope includes Oman 76.5%, Rivita 51%, WMC 55%, Enovation 85% and Prime 51% at March; Tierra was added/restructured afterward. Indian GAAP AS is used, not IndAS; Oman IFRS figures are aligned with stated exceptions. Financial opening is 31 March 2026, latest P&L 30 June; subsequent cash is modeled, not observed. Horizon 19 October 2026–19 October 2031, nominal pretax, no dividends, 15% hurdle with 12%/18% alternatives. ₹5 lakh is an illustrative liquidity test, not an allocation recommendation. High confidence covers printed balances, issued shares and official historical trades; comparable growth, capital returns and governance are Medium; current funding/NCI-dependent equity valuation is Low. Forecast uncertainty remains distinct. G1/G2/G4 Conditional; G3 Hold—unresolved.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5 and EARN 6 have claim-linked reasons in the factor audit. BQS=0.20×5+0.20×5+0.12×8+0.10×6+0.12×5+0.10×3+0.08×4+0.08×5=5.18. GQS raw=0.40×8+0.20×6+0.15×6+0.15×5+0.10×3=6.35, capped 5.00 for persistent CASH 3. REV’s numerical starting 9 is capped 8 for Medium confidence and three relevant comparable years; no factor 9–10 is awarded. IAS retains Q=5.18, D3 and L7; R/P are NS because material funding and owner-attribution inputs are unsupported. Known IAS contribution 2.595, coverage 55%, full-scale bounds 3.045–7.095, not a reweighted score. Quality/Growth ranking is allowed, IAS ranking is not. Half-up one-decimal displays are 5.2/5.0/NS. These transparent scoring heuristics are not validated return predictors.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Felix designs and supplies water/wastewater plants, membranes and treatment systems; executes EPC and BOOT/BOO projects; and provides operation/maintenance and waste-recovery services. The newer group also operates Oman used-oil/oily-sludge recovery, hazardous-waste handling and Indian recycling/metals businesses. Goods and services are recognized on transfer/performance under contract policies; collections can lag reported earnings substantially. FY26 group goods revenue ₹63.2525 crore and services ₹38.9597 crore replaced FY25 mix ₹9.2607/27.5612 crore. Parent goods are specifically water plants/equipment/systems/membranes, not assumed all metals trading:₹42.8045 crore; parent services ₹34.5542 crore. Group customer-location revenue ₹81.9153 crore India and ₹20.2972 crore Oman makes domestic revenue 80.14%; substantial fixed assets sit in Oman. A single accounting operating segment does not imply economically identical returns across these activities. It is a capital-and-working-capital-intensive project/asset platform, not an asset-light pure engineering annuity. Acquired Tierra is a later perimeter change, not FY26 revenue.

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: A plausible advantage is combining engineering, process integration, water reuse and onsite operation with difficult waste-handling know-how. Mechanism: successful commissioning and operating qualifications can reduce customer switching and delivery risk. Evidence: BOOT assets, the Oman facility and a disclosed three-year OQ8 agreement. Durability is less established: customer concentration, renewals, bid-win rates, realized treatment fees, price premiums, uptime penalties and independently measured technology advantages are not disclosed sufficiently. Failure mode is a project delay, poor utilization or squeezed treatment/commodity realization while capital remains tied up. Wabag’s municipal/industrial-water and desalination scale, Ion Exchange’s engineering plus resins/membranes/chemicals mix, and Concord Enviro’s industrial-water/ZLD systems provide relevant context, not identical comparables. Concord’s FY26 report shows ₹557.856 crore sales and ₹36.626 crore adjusted EBITDA, illustrating that water-sector labels do not guarantee Felix’s proposed 30% margin. No synchronized peer price multiples or unverifiable market-share percentage is imported. MOAT 5 recognizes useful but contestable execution capability.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Parent revenue FY20–FY26 is ₹1.8676/2.9546/12.3825/19.3804/28.8603/30.6888/77.3587 crore. The five-year FY21–FY26 CAGR 92.13% begins in a disrupted trough and is not the scored window. Chosen three-year FY23–FY26 parent CAGR 58.63% uses the same legal parent and water-equipment/services franchise; annual additions FY24/FY25/FY26 are ₹9.4799/1.8285/46.6699 crore. It is not labeled a clean group organic-volume CAGR: project timing, price/mix, intercompany sales and activity expansion are not fully separated. Parent services rose from ₹19.6952 to 34.5542 crore, and parent water goods/projects ₹10.9936 to 42.8045 crore, supporting genuine breadth beyond a mere new subsidiary consolidation. Group revenue ₹33.9048/36.8219/102.2125 crore FY24–26 spans changing subsidiaries; FY26 growth 177.59% is reported, not presumed organic. Q1 FY27 revenue ₹28.2210 versus ₹20.6198 crore is+36.86%; TTM ₹109.8137 crore. This single quarter does not earn a trajectory bonus. Volume, realization and fully comparable ten-year CAGR are ND.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Water reuse, treatment compliance and waste recovery give a plausible recurring demand base, but addressability requires permits, feedstock/customers, uptime and collections. The May 22 OQ8 disclosure covers three years with estimated OMR 2.6 million service value; actual quantities/types and recovered-product proceeds vary, so it is not a fully reconciled guaranteed cash backlog. June 6 management targeted FY27 sales ₹180–200 crore, EBITDA 30–31%, Oman ₹60–70 crore and ramping 40 TPD toward full utilization in 3–6 months. Metals/plastics/acid-reclamation plans are separately less proven. The base uses ₹150/180/210/235/260 crore FY27–31, then ₹280 crore FY32 run-rate, below near-term guidance; margins 26/26/25/25/24/24%, WC 58%→50% of revenue and cash capex ₹10/12/14/15/15/16 crore. Those assumptions still need new funding and substantial collection improvement. There is no verified capacity-to-sales unit bridge across heterogeneous segments. Broad committed capital rose ₹118.9072→217.2479 crore; incremental normalized after-tax operating return 14.26% is around an explicitly analytical 14–18% capital-cost range, not exceptional. Current cash realization caps GQS at 5 rather than allowing ambitious growth guidance to offset weak self-funding.

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Ritesh Patel leads the group; March 31 promoters held 50.78%. That dated pattern discloses 3,535,295 promoter shares pledged, 40.46% of promoter holdings; the Mufin loan requires pledge coverage 2.5× its balance. This is financing risk, not a misconduct conclusion. FY26 Ritesh remuneration lines total ₹1.3164 crore versus ₹0.2590 crore the prior year; the board states remuneration complied with approvals. Related-party dealings, investments, loans and guarantees are explicitly disclosed, but value and recoverability still need independent economics. FY26 cash from warrant calls ₹46.3565 crore accompanied ₹4.8434 crore issue expenses. All 936,650 unexercised old warrants lapsed 27 August 2025;₹4.0983 crore forfeiture reserve is past received money, not future funding. Actual shares increased 25.84% from 13,673,070 to 17,206,350.

The annual audit is unmodified, with emphasis on unprovided doubtful debts, loans/advances, investments and warrant accounting; management expects recovery and says the relevant accounting reflects its assessments. The October 15 secretarial report records a 23-day FY25 results delay and ₹135,700 fine, waived by NSE 22 September 2025, and a one-day annual-report delay/₹2,360 fine paid; management reports no further adverse action pending. Other annual-report filing delays are described with corrective filings, not treated as proven concealment. S.N. Shah’s term completion and SNDK’s proposed five-year appointment are ordinary rotation, not an asserted auditor resignation. Finance director Nishant Sharma resigned 30 September for other professional commitments. Milestones: FY26 parent/group revenue scale-up achieved; June Oman utilization/FY27 targets not yet verified; August direct Tierra acquisition target 5 September versus completion 8 October shows a delay but completion. A migration application is not an achieved main-board move. GOV/EXEC 5 reflect the mixed record without unsupported allegations.

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 reported group PAT ₹18.1827 crore, PBT ₹26.6956 crore and core operating EBIT ₹26.2030 crore differ: other income ₹3.6628 crore, interest ₹3.1596 crore and associate loss ₹0.0106 crore are normalized explicitly. Core EBITDA is ₹28.2182 crore; EBIT/finance cost 8.29×. Group CFO begins with ₹26.6956 crore PBT; adds D&A₹2.0152, finance ₹3.1596, preliminary expense ₹0.0255, supplier impairment ₹0.5239, associate loss ₹0.0106, expected-credit-loss ₹0.5225 and translation reserve ₹2.5294; subtracts interest income ₹1.4904 to reach ₹33.9919 crore before working capital. The listed asset/claim movements produce −₹33.7501 crore before cash taxes ₹2.8412 crore and CFO −₹36.5914 crore. Cash PPE spending ₹14.6170 crore is separate investing cash: CFO−capex=−₹51.2084 crore, before financing-classified interest. FY24–26 reported CFO/PAT is-1.2488×. This broad CFO includes financial loans, member receivables and capital creditor movements, so it is not asserted to be a pure trade cash-conversion ratio. Debt/equity and creditor financing, not accounting profit, fund the expansion.

Opening cash ₹9.8195 crore includes ₹4.0098 crore margin deposits, leaving ₹5.8097 crore available before entity-access restrictions. Ordinary recoverable WC ₹60.0864 crore explicitly includes inventory, receivables, supplier/employee advances, GST credit/prepayments/accruals less operating creditors, customer/statutory balances and expense provisions. Capital creditors ₹26.8716 crore, old current tax ₹8.3361 crore, legacy gratuity ₹0.3480 crore and debt ₹33.8660 crore are separate claims. Advance-tax/TDS ₹0.7372 crore and GST-refund ₹0.8767 crore are separately recovered once. Corporate/associate loans ₹48.5208 crore and unreceived Oman member capital ₹13.9149 crore are not unrestricted cash. All ₹0.9218 crore disclosed doubtful receivables are excluded from recoverable model value once; management has not provided against them because it expects recovery. Capital advance ₹2.5 crore becomes PPE without a second cash payment. Deferred-tax ₹0.9322 crore is retained as a terminal claim; leases remain debt.

Presentation differences are explicitly bounded: FY25 group CFO starts ₹11.0861 crore versus P&L PBT ₹11.9948 crore; FY26 parent CFO starts group PBT ₹26.6956 rather than parent ₹28.1879 crore. A₹5 crore borrowing/loan cash classification difference is two-sided, not evidence of missing money. Group owner-profit reserve credit and NCI notes need attribution reconciliation. Q1 group PAT ₹5.5129 plus minority loss adjustment ₹0.1619 gives ownerPAT ₹5.6748; printed ₹3.20 EPS uses pre-NCI profit, whereas ownerPAT/current shares gives ₹3.2981. FY25 printed diluted EPS/denominator also does not simply reconcile. We use current shares and owner profit, not those denominators. Broad average-capital operating ROIC 11.69% and incremental 14.26% are transparent mixed-cohort proxies; uncommissioned assets and advances remain in capital.

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Price ₹188 implies ₹323.47938 crore equity value, FY26 owner-PAT P/E 17.83× and current-share TTM owner P/E 15.87×. A March gross-debt less available-cash EV proxy ₹351.5357 crore is not a clean groupEV: book NCI is not market-value NCI, non-operating assets and post-March cash/debt are unresolved. Hence no false exact group EV/EBITDA or point fair value is stated.

The 67-month diagnostic starts March 31 balances, anchors actual Q1 sales/core EBITDA/D&A/finance expense, then models WC stocks, new capex, debt interest/amortization, old creditors/taxes/gratuity, loan collections, acquisitions and dilution. Cash tax 29% of positive operating pretax profit is an assumption with no immediate loss refund. Mufin’s₹0.2448155 crore monthly EMI determines its implied rate; other rates are explicit assumptions. Axis’s inconsistent date/remaining-installment wording is modeled from disclosed current maturity over 17 remaining months, with a 10-month accelerated sensitivity. Existing CC renewal is assumed, not newly sanctioned cash. Tierra’s₹12 crore external acquisition is one cash cost including ₹10 crore old liabilities; the subsequent intragroup ₹1.686714 crore is not another group outflow. New Tierra capital ₹4.531464 crore is ring-fenced to its project, not freely available to the parent. No unreceived member contribution or expired warrant supplies cash.

Without new money, bear/base/bull have maximum running gaps ₹48.60/₹33.07/₹19.08 crore and no IRR. Conditional alternatives allow up to ₹40 crore hypothetical cumulative new debt at 12%, amortizing after month 30, and only post-cutoff rescue equity at ₹150/share plus 3% issue costs. Bear/base/bull funded IRRs are-16.23%/11.07%/31.53%; bear needs ₹31.66 crore equity and base ₹39.80 crore debt. None proves such financing was available.

Base terminal FY32 run-rate EBITDA ₹67.20 crore×9=EV ₹604.80 crore; less debt ₹14.7120 and remaining claims ₹0.9322, plus cash ₹15.4934, financial-asset recovery ₹14.7505 and restricted-margin release ₹2.0049, gives group net equity ₹621.4047 crore. Assumed common ownership 88% gives ₹546.8361 crore/1.720635 crore shares=₹317.81; no second book-NCI deduction. Common fractions 80/88/90% are explicit scenario estimates, not verified equity allocation. Therefore R/P/IAS are NS despite complete diagnostics. The base 15% entry ₹158.02 is conditional arithmetic, not a recommended buy price. At 9×, the 15% reverse hurdle needs FY27 ₹179.61 crore and terminal ₹335.27 crore sales plus ₹8.08 crore hypothetical equity; no funded 18% crossing is found within 0.30–3.00× revenue-path scan because early funding constraints break monotonicity. The attached two-variable growth/multiple grid, loan-recovery, claim-timing, rates, capex and ownership sensitivities show what drives the answer. A point DCF would merely disguise the same unverified funding/NCI assumptions.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that expanding sales and accounting profit do not become accessible parent-shareholder cash before creditor, tax, acquisition and debt claims fall due. Low recovery of ₹48.52 crore financial advances, slower customer collections, underutilized Oman/BOOT assets and margin normalization can require adverse equity issuance. The conditional bear uses FY27 ₹110 crore revenue, 20% EBITDA margin, WC 68% and ₹7 crore capex, then modest growth; it produces ₹77.58 terminal value per diluted share and-16.23% IRR despite substantial rescue funding. Refusing the rescue removes the IRR, not the cash gap.

The essential-survival test stops discretionary expansion, uses ₹3 crore annual maintenance, ₹100 crore FY27 revenue and 20% margin, but retains old taxes, capital creditors, debt and the already-completed acquisition. With delayed loan recovery it has ₹37.24 crore modeled gap; a 75%-collection-in-six-months countercase with lower WC survives without rescue. The available filings do not establish which post-March collections and cash actually occurred, so G3 remains Hold—unresolved, not a demonstrated Fail or a Pass based on hypothetical facilities. A full ₹48 crore associate-guarantee call plus depressed sales/margins is a remote boundary (₹94.69 crore gap), not asserted probable stress or actual default. The Oman guarantee is a group borrowing support, not a second charge on top of the same drawn debt. Thesis-break variables are accessible cash, recovery timing and debt/drawing-power obligations, not sales alone.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: From ₹188, 5×/10× in five years requires ₹940/1,880 per share and approximately 37.97%/58.49% annual price growth with no dividends. At unchanged 1.720635 crore shares, that means owner equity ₹1,617.40/3,234.79 crore; dilution raises the required business value. Holding the base’s 88% owner fraction, 9× terminal EBITDA margin 24% and net non-operating bridge constant, the required terminal revenue is roughly ₹843/1,694 crore, far above the ₹280 crore base and ₹430 crore bull. This is algebra, not a forecast: sustained capital funding, large capacity/customer expansion and parent cash realization would all be needed. A low initial market cap or management’s near-term growth target does not establish a 5×/10× outcome.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: 1. Recoveries of corporate/associate advances: baseline ₹48.5208 crore; request dated receipts, counterparties, terms and remaining ageing before treating them as funding. 2. Actual unrestricted cash by entity and bank drawing power: baseline March₹5.8097 crore group before access restrictions; any unsupported reliance on fresh facilities blocks implementation. 3. Capital-creditor ₹26.8716 crore/current-tax ₹8.3361 crore settlement and maturity schedule: validate payments without double-counting WC. 4. Revenue, core EBITDA and cash by water/BOOT, Oman and metals/Tierra: compare FY27 guidance ₹180–200 crore with Q1 ₹28.221 crore and cash receipts, not just orders. 5. Oman 40 TPD utilization and OQ8 contract volumes/fees: verify the June 3–6 month ramp milestone and necessary permissions. 6. Total share count, subsidiary minority interests and new raises: reconcile Tierra direct/indirect ownership and acquired liabilities; treat unreceived money as unavailable. 7. Net operating cash after separating financial advances and capital-creditor movements: require sustained positive conversion, not a single release. 8. Receivable ageing, margin deposits, pledged promoter shares and covenant/renewal status: investigate deterioration, not presume default. 9. Cash-flow/NCI/EPS reconciliation and later auditor reports: assess exact scope and company response. 10. Liquidity, lot size and current surveillance before any proposed position. These are research review triggers, not scheduled monitoring or trading instructions.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: Hold—unresolved funding and owner-attribution evidence; speculative scaling/special-situation watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder. BQS 5.18 and capped GQS 5.0 are scoreable historical judgments. IAS remains NS; its diagnostic base does not become a price target or a recommendation. No severe integrity failure or actual default is asserted, and no blanket financial-reliability failure is inferred from a handful of bounded presentation differences. A verified current cash/debt/claim roll-forward, collections of advances, subsidiary-level economics and owner attribution could turn this into a scoreable investment case; weaker collections or unaffordable essential maturities could instead establish a gate failure. A lower quoted price alone does not cure missing funding evidence. Position sizing or execution would require live liquidity and the user’s circumstances;₹5 lakh is only the common research reference.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The linked source register separates audited annuals, signed interim/transaction filings, management guidance, official market data and peer context. Printed amounts are converted from ₹lakh to ₹crore by÷100. Group/parent and original/comparative labels are retained; no vendor snapshot substitutes for current financials. High-confidence printed numbers do not imply high-confidence recoverability. Main assumptions are future sales/margins, WC stocks, capex, tax 29%, new finance 12%, facility renewal, loan recoveries, creditor dates, terminal multiple 6/9/12, common equity fraction 80/88/90%, financial-asset haircuts and margin-deposit release. Current tax credits/GST refunds and old obligations each have one claim treatment. Financing failure is retained, with no IRR on negative-cash paths. Open evidence: post-March accessible cash/debt, contractual recoveries and claim due dates; acquired Tierra balance sheet and final full ownership; NCI allocation/statement reconciliation; customer-level cohorts/concentration and project-level return/maintenance requirements; accepted current rating, if any; executable depth/spread and later exchange actions. No unrelated Felix Generics/Healthcare rating is attributed to this issuer. Read-only searches cannot establish universal legal clearance. The dated public sources support the specific statements, not every future assumption.

GOV.reason: Unmodified audits and explicit disclosures support adequate conduct, but large non-operating advances, related-party deployment, 40.46% promoter encumbrance and rapidly changing subsidiary perimeter constrain stewardship confidence. Fines were waived/paid, not live unresolved sanctions. No severe-integrity finding is established.

MOAT.reason: Engineering execution, process integration, BOOT/O&M and hazardous-waste qualification are useful and contestable capabilities. No verified retention, pricing premium or durable excess-return series supports a stronger structural-moat score.

REV.reason: Three-year parent water-equipment/services revenue CAGR 58.63% starts 9, capped 8 for Medium confidence and short relevant comparable scaling history. Parent services grew 75.45% and water equipment/projects 289.36% FY26, supporting breadth beyond acquired consolidation. Project timing/price/volume remain unresolved. No extra current-quarter bonus and no additional small-base penalty.

DUR.reason: OQ8 waste-management agreement and ongoing water-reuse/BOOT activity provide tangible demand access. Capacity funding, utilization, chemical/metals diversification and customer-level concentration constrain accessible duration; TAM alone is not scored.

CAP.reason: Broad incremental post-tax return proxy 14.26% is around the analytical 14–18% capital-cost range, not exceptional. Including capital creditors and advances avoids flattering returns by omitting deployed capital. New asset cohorts and acquisitions have no independently proven unit IRRs.

CASH.reason: Cash conversion is persistently weak or volatile across the reported profitable history, and ₹48.52 crore non-operating loans/advances plus unpaid capital claims tie up liquidity. Reported CFO classifications are not falsely equated with pure trade conversion. Even after considering investment classification, realized funding relies heavily on equity/credit; stable self-funded cash generation has not been established.

BAL.reason: Debt ₹33.87 crore includes leases; available March cash only ₹5.81 crore versus capital creditors ₹26.87 crore/current tax ₹8.34 crore, as well as guarantees and future acquisition cash. Existing loans can support a surviving collection case, but current liquidity and covenant/drawing power are not verified. This is funding fragility, not an observed default.

EXEC.reason: Group and parent revenue scaled and Tierra restructuring completed in October, later than the August filing’s September target. Oman ramp and later metals/plastics ambitions are not validated as achieved. Some concrete delivery, insufficient repeatable cash-backed milestone record.

EARN.reason: FY26 operating EBIT grows strongly after removing other income; current-share owner TTM earnings improve. Large changing perimeter, goods/service mix, sharply higher group margins, EPS/NCI presentation differences and dilution limit a higher recurrence/per-share-quality assessment. CASH is scored separately.

R.reason: Current cash, actual committed financing, acquired liabilities and economic NCI attribution remain materially unverified. The 11.07% conditional base is a diagnostic, not a supported scoreable return.

D.reason: Material downside and adverse recapitalization are supported by the matched stress alternatives: funded bear IRR−16.23% requires ₹40 crore hypothetical debt and ₹31.66 crore equity; no-rescue growth paths have cash gaps. A collections-led restrained countercase survives, so uncertainty is not converted into proven ordinary-stress insolvency.

P.reason: Conditional reverse hurdles and multiple sensitivities are calculated, but subsidiary cash/NCI and actual funding uncertainty prevent a defensible point assessment of priced-in owner expectations.

L.reason: Starting lower-band 9 for 1.42 days at 5% is downgraded 2 for ₹94,000 lot granularity, concentrated participation and official irregular-trading/ended-market-making cautions. Historical capacity is observable; live depth remains unverified, not automaticallyNS.

Actual unrestricted cash by entity and bank drawing power: baseline March₹5.8097 crore group before access restrictions; any unsupported reliance on fresh facilities blocks implementation. 3. Capital-creditor ₹26.8716 crore/current-tax ₹8.3361 crore settlement and maturity schedule: validate payments without double-counting WC. 4. Revenue, core EBITDA and cash by water/BOOT, Oman and metals/Tierra: compare FY27 guidance ₹180–200 crore with Q1 ₹28.221 crore and cash receipts, not just orders. 5. Oman 40 TPD utilization and OQ8 contract volumes/fees: verify the June 3–6 month ramp milestone and necessary permissions. 6. Total share count, subsidiary minority interests and new raises: reconcile Tierra direct/indirect ownership and acquired liabilities; treat unreceived money as unavailable. 7. Net operating cash after separating financial advances and capital-creditor movements: require sustained positive conversion, not a single release. 8. Receivable ageing, margin deposits, pledged promoter shares and covenant/renewal status: investigate deterioration, not presume default. 9. Cash-flow/NCI/EPS reconciliation and later auditor reports: assess exact scope and company response. 10. Liquidity, lot size and current surveillance before any proposed position. These are research review triggers, not scheduled monitoring or trading instructions.
